claims.claim: Cyprian was born around the beginning of the 3rd century and died on September 14, 258.
Cyprian was elected bishop of Carthage in 248 or 249.
On the Unity of the Church was written in A.D. 251.

The treatise was written on the occasion of the schism of Novatian, to keep back the Carthaginians from him, because Novatus and some other presbyters of Cyprian's church had originated the whole disturbance.
The treatise has been subjected to falsifying interpolations, long since exposed and detected, to make it less subversive of the countertheory of Rome as developed by the school doctors.
The treatise is important as a key to the entire writings of Cyprian, because this theory is everywhere the underlying principle of his conduct and of his correspondence.
The treatise illustrates the epistles of Ignatius as well as Cyprian's own, and gives the sense in which the primitive Christians understood the words of the Creed, 'the Holy Catholic Church.'

Cyprian was a Christian theologian and bishop of Carthage who led the Christians of North Africa during a period of persecution from Rome, and upon his execution he became the first bishop-martyr of Africa.
Cyprian was born of wealthy pagan parents and was educated in law, practicing as a lawyer in Carthage before converting to Christianity about 246.
Cyprian's letters and tracts are a major source for the emperor Decius' persecution.
In 256–7 Cyprian's theology led to a split with Rome, whose bishop Stephen recognized the baptism of Novatianus' community.
